questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x-4,\, & 2\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{2}^{3}x\cdot (2x-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}(2{x}^{2}-4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-2{x}^{2})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot (2x-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}(2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3})|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{43}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{43}{6}-{(\frac{8}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=1.9,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{8}, & 1\le x<5, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot 2{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{6}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}|}_{1}^{5} \\  & =5.5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =5.5-{(1.9)}^{2} \\  & =1.89.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=4$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{27}, & 0<x<3, \\ \frac{9-x}{27}, & 3\le x<9, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{9}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{9}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2x}{27}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{9}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{27}(9-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{2{x}^{3}}{27}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{9}\frac{1}{27}(9{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{54}|}_{0}^{3}+{\frac{1}{27}(3{x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})|}_{3}^{9} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}+\frac{81}{4}-\frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{39}{2}-{4}^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{2},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{4{x}^{3}},\, & 1<x<3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{9}{4{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{9}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{9}{4}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{4}-{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{4}-\frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{7}{8},$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{3(x-1)}{{x}^{5}},\, & x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3(x-1)}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3{x}^{2}}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3x-3}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}+(-\frac{3}{x}+\frac{3}{2{x}^{2}}){|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+3-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}-{(\frac{7}{8})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{63}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$
